tldr: At the propensity boundary \(e_{n,\lambda}(x)=x^{1+\lambda/\log n}/2\), regular QTE efficiency breaks at \(r_n=\sqrt{\log n/n}\), but global smoothness permits optimal boundary transport and residual centering. The exact Hellinger-local minimax variance is \(2p_0(1-p_0)B(\lambda)/f_1(q_1)^2\); a feasible two-fold augmented-CDF QTE root attains it in squared risk and yields a data-only studentizer with uniformly honest ninety-percent Wald intervals. In the legal local experiment every regular limiting normalized error law is the convolution of the sharp Gaussian law with a probability law, without a moment premise; finite second moments are required only for the resulting variance inequality. At \(\lambda=0\), the fixed design \(e(X)=X/2\) is an index-two law with infinite inverse-propensity mean, and only the all-estimator converse transfers to the declared larger local models.
